messages:
Maria: Heads-up — our model-serving svc in us-west-2 is showing extreme skew, 4 pods getting ~80% of traffic, others almost idle. Users see retries + 500s from the overloaded pods.
Josh: I see increased pod-level retries in the grafana traces, and TCP retransmits on the host NICs. Which scheduler are we using for the service?
Devon: ipvs with rr by default for that ClusterIP service. It's the large g4/g5 GPU pool behind it.
Maria: Dumped ipvs state — endpoints and weights look fine, but flows stick to a few endpoints. Posted output below.
Maria: ```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats
IP Virtual Server version: 1.2.1
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> 10.10.3.12:8080      rr  Masq
  -> 10.10.3.13:8080      rr  Masq
  -> 10.10.3.14:8080      rr  Masq
  -> 10.10.3.15:8080      rr  Masq
Traffic: 123456 total packets 98765 total bytes
  10.10.3.12 packets: 99000 bytes: 80000000
  10.10.3.13 packets: 2000 bytes: 1600000
  10.10.3.14 packets: 1500 bytes: 1200000
  10.10.3.15 packets: 956 bytes: 800000
```
Anya: That's wild. Could be L4 offload / connection affinity at kernel/NIC level. Any MTU/TSO/GSO/SG settings changed on those nodes recently?
Josh: We rolled a driver update on 3 hosts yesterday (firmware 21.4.3 -> 21.5.0) in us-west-2a. They are the 3 with heavy traffic per ipvs stats — suspicious.
Devon: Also seeing higher packet drop counters on NIC RX for the hot nodes: ethtool -S shows rx_missed, and netstat -s shows TCP retransmits.
Maria: Workaround I applied: cycled kube-proxy on one hot node — flows redistributed. Restarting kube-proxy seems to clear the stuck flows temporarily.
Anya: That's consistent with ipvs connection table entries being long-lived; kube-proxy restart flushes ipvs conntrack. But doesn't fix root cause.
Josh: Could be hardware offload + GSO/TSO interaction + a kernel bug where large packets get dropped and flows back off to same endpoint. Also possible RDMA devices interfering with kernel hashing on NIC? We do have p2p RDMA enabled on those GPU nodes.
Devon: Repro steps: 1) hit service with many small concurrent connections 2) watch ipvsadm stats 3) observe that dstip distribution quickly concentrates on certain endpoints.
Maria: Action items: 1) roll back driver on a canary hot node to previous firmware and monitor; 2) flip off GRO/GSO on one node to see effect; 3) collect tcpdump + gso/skbuff counters; 4) open ticket with NIC vendor.
Anya: Also add a kube-proxy config change test — switch ipvs scheduler to lc (least-conn) for that service and see if stickiness improves. Patch suggestion below.
Anya: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: kube-proxy-config
data:
  mode: "ipvs"
  ipvsScheduler: "lc"
```
Josh: For risk management, we should also add a temporary ingress-level fallback: route a small % of traffic to a warm standby pool in us-west-2b using Service topology / headless + external load balancer. Reduces tail risk while we debug.
Devon: Logging note: we saw many retries from the client with connection reset by peer and some ECONNABORTED. Might be kernel dropping because of packet size mismatch (MTU). The hot nodes are on jumbo MTU 9000; others are 1500 — we recently had cross-subnet changes.
Maria: Confirmed: heavy nodes are in the 9000-MTU VLAN; others 1500. Could be GSO causing large L4 segments that are mishandled by offload on the updated drivers.
Anya: Short-term mitigation: align MTU across pool (set 1500) on canary and retest, or disable GSO: `ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off`.
Josh: I'll schedule a rolling canary: rollback NIC driver on g4-03, disable GSO, restart kube-proxy, run load test. Will report back in 30m.
infra-bot: Incident alert created: #INC-2026-1473 — svc imbalance in us-west-2 GPU pool. Linked to thread.
Maria: Thanks. Also capture `conntrack -L` and ipvs conn table before and after restarts for our postmortem.
Devon: If vendor confirms bug, we should add kernel param tweak to avoid ipvs conn mangle: `net.ipv4.tcp_no_metrics_save=1` maybe helps. But we'll wait for repro.
Josh: Update: canary rollback looks promising — traffic rebalanced after driver rollback + kube-proxy restart. No retries in next 15m. Still collecting packets for vendor.
Maria: Great. We'll keep fallback routes primed until vendor root cause/driver fix. Posting logs to the incident doc. :thumbsup:
